- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate prices in the latter part of the forecast horizon; adjust upward for persistent downward trends or mean reversion.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes; cap forecast values at 1–2% below the peak immediately preceding the spike.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; dampen forecast sensitivity to short-term noise.
- Mean reversion bias: if history shows strong recent trend, forecast should gradually revert toward historical average over 10–15 days.
- Lagged response: forecast often lags true price movements by 2–5 days; adjust for delayed reaction in the first 5–7 days of forecast.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values; if last 5–7 days are high, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overestimation.
